title: Raga Bihagra
hook: a raga for late at night, colored by separation

segments.voice: Yesterday, listening in Devgandhari, and your line was twice, slowly. Did a second reading change a reply? Today the week ends, and the day does too. Day one thousand seventy-eight.

The house is asleep. The dishes are done, the phone is face down, and the only light is a lamp or a streetlight through the curtain. At this hour some people find themselves talking to their own heart, quietly, the way you'd talk to a child who can't sleep. Daytime is loud enough to drown that voice out; night isn't. The Granth has a raga for this hour, and in it a Guru speaks to his own soul. This week began at dawn, with the hope of Asa. It ends here, at night. Today: Raga Bihagra.
screen: `THE HOUSE IS ASLEEP.` → `TALKING TO ONE'S OWN HEART.` → `FROM DAWN TO NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Bihagra is a night raga. Tradition sets it for the late hours, and its mood is colored by separation, the ache of being apart from the one you love. In the Guru Granth Sahib, that ache has a direction. The beloved is God, and the one waiting is the soul. Guru Ram Das has chants in Bihagra that keep calling out to the singer's own soul with a tender word, jindurie, something like my dear life, my little soul. The chants urge it, again and again, toward the Name. It's the way a person might talk to themselves late at night, gently, when sleep won't come: come on, dear one, remember what matters. Notice this isn't despair. In these chants, separation is a kind of love. You only miss what you're bound to. The longing itself is the sign that the bond is real, and the hymns turn the ache into a reason to remember. Now look back at the week, because the ragas made a day. Asa met the dawn with hope, and opened with a hymn that hears all creation singing at God's door. Gujri, quiet devotion, with a crane flying far while her chicks are cared for. Devgandhari, gentle, a Guru admitting that the mind won't listen, and a short hymn heard twice. And now Bihagra, at night, longing. The same Word, through different hours. Today's line: night longing.
screen: `A NIGHT RAGA, COLORED BY SEPARATION.` · `JINDURIE: MY DEAR LIFE.` · `LONGING MEANS THE BOND IS REAL.` · `THE WEEK: DAWN, QUIET, GENTLE, NIGHT.` · then, large: `NIGHT LONGING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to the gaps in the night. Sit, and dim whatever you can, the screen, the lights, your eyes. Breathe slowly. Late sounds come far apart: a car a long way off, the house settling, a pipe ticking. Don't reach for them. Let the silence between them be part of what you hear. If a longing rises in one of those gaps, let it come, and let it settle back into the quiet without chasing it. If you pray, you can set one Waheguru into a gap. If you don't, simply rest in the spaces. Tonight, if you're up late, play one Bihagra shabad in the dark. The bell holds the time.
Raga Bihagra. A night raga colored by separation, where Guru Ram Das calls to his own soul as my dear life. Today's word.

Your line: night longing. Before you sleep tonight, give your own heart a tender name, the way the chant does, and tell it one thing worth remembering. Day one thousand seventy-eight. A week of ragas, done.

howItsDone: Shabads headed Bihagra are sung in that raga in kirtan, and tradition places it in the late hours of the night; its chants by Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan are sung as songs of the soul's longing for God.
